hero.title: The ATS analysis you will never do by hand again.
hero.lead: Every application starts from scratch: re-reading the job offer, guessing the keywords, rewriting the same sentences. Talento locks in the decisions — extraction, semantic matching, scoring, interview prep — and replays them on every offer in a single pass.
hero.audience: For people aiming at one specific job, not fifty.

problem.total: Estimated time lost: ~12 hours per application (1.5 days)
problem.title: Tailoring a resume to a job offer costs a day. Every time.
problem.p1: It is never the easy part that hurts. It is re-reading the offer line by line to guess what the filter expects. It is rewriting the same experience under a different job title. It is the PDF the ATS parses badly, and the automatic rejection before a human ever opens the file.
problem.p2: Nobody counts those hours, and everyone pays them again on the next application.
sinks: Re-read the offer and isolate the real criteria
Rewrite the resume for the job title
Guess the keywords the filter expects
Check that the PDF survives parsing
Start all over on the next application

method.title: Every decision already made. So you can go straight to the interview.
method.lead: A resume builder gives you templates. Here, you get decisions: how the offer is broken down, how a skill is recognized as equivalent, which gaps matter, in what order results reach the screen. Set once, applied to every analysis. That is what makes the model useful: an unconstrained LLM improvises, an LLM inside a fixed structure produces results you can compare from one offer to the next.

decisions.title: A single pass
decisions.body: The offer and the resume go out together in one structured call. No prompt chain, no stacked latency: the first answer arrives in under two seconds.

decisions.title: Semantic matching
decisions.body: “Vue 3” and “Vue.js”, “Postgres” and “PostgreSQL”, “fluent English” and “bilingual” are recognized as equivalent. Intent matters, not the exact string.

decisions.title: Five gap categories
decisions.body: Technical skills, soft skills, languages, experience level, degrees and certifications. The same boxes on every analysis, with the same matching threshold.

decisions.title: Ready-to-paste rewrites
decisions.body: Every weak or missing criterion gets a results-oriented wording, readable by an ATS and a recruiter alike, that you paste straight into your document.

decisions.title: Interview built from the gap
decisions.body: Questions do not come from a generic bank: they are generated from the exact difference between your profile and the offer, with feedback on every answer.

decisions.title: Results as they stream
decisions.body: Criteria appear one by one through an SSE stream. You read the first results while the next ones arrive, with no loading screen.

decisions.title: Data control
decisions.body: Files are not archived beyond the session. Gemini receives the text for the analysis; signed-in accounts can keep a history. No resume is ever sold, and you can delete everything from your profile.

items.question: What stack is it built on?
items.answer: Vue 3, TypeScript, Pinia and Tailwind on the frontend. FastAPI, PostgreSQL and the Gemini model via google-genai on the backend. Docker deployment on Railway.

items.question: How is it different from resume builders?
items.answer: A builder gives you a layout. Here, you get a diagnosis: what the offer asks for, what your resume actually covers, what is missing, and what to write instead.

items.question: Are my documents stored?
items.answer: The resume and the offer are sent to Google Gemini for the analysis, then processed in memory on the server. For signed-in accounts, the history (analyses, interview simulations, cover letters) can be saved. Only your account (and that history) is stored long-term; you can delete everything from your profile. Details: Privacy page.

items.question: Do you use analytics tools?
items.answer: Yes. PostHog (EU region) measures product usage and errors. Once you sign in, your account can be linked to events. See the privacy policy.

items.question: Does Talento also write the cover letter?
items.answer: Yes, for signed-in accounts. The cover letter module writes a targeted letter (hook, body, closing) from your resume and the job offer, in the tone, length and language you choose. It relies only on your resume: review it before sending. Copy or export it as .txt / .md, and find it again in your dashboard history.

items.question: What if Talento's AI quota runs out?
items.answer: Connect your own API key from your profile: Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Your analyses then go through your provider, which bills you directly. The key is encrypted, never displayed again, and you can switch back to Talento at any time.

items.question: Is the score reliable?
items.answer: It is an estimate calibrated on the criteria extracted from the offer, not the exact score of a proprietary ATS. It helps you prioritize your fixes, not predict a hire.

items.question: Can I host the project myself?
items.answer: Yes. The repository is public under the MIT License and includes the Dockerfiles, the getting-started guide and the required environment variables.

items.question: How can I contribute?
items.answer: Issues and pull requests are open. The contributing guide covers the local setup, commit conventions and the review process.
